reproducibilityChecklist.rule: Split only along the declared distribution axis (seed, fold, subject block) — never by arm or by comparison.
reproducibilityChecklist.why: every comparison subtracts two arms; splitting there puts the subtraction across a hardware boundary

reproducibilityChecklist.rule: Derive each unit's seed from the unit id alone: int(sha256(unit_id).hexdigest()[:8], 16) % 2**31 — never from the account, the shard index or the launch order.
reproducibilityChecklist.why: a unit then reruns identically wherever and whenever it lands

reproducibilityChecklist.rule: Every account clones the same published commit.
Every account installs the same pinned requirements file; record its digest as requirementsDigest.
reproducibilityChecklist.why: a library update changes numerics silently

reproducibilityChecklist.rule: Request the same accelerator model (machine_shape) for every account and stamp the one that actually arrived.
reproducibilityChecklist.why: different GPU models produce different floating-point results, so shards stamped with different accelerators are refused at merge

reproducibilityChecklist.rule: Each shard writes python, torch, CUDA, cuDNN, accelerator name, commit, requirements digest, data checksum and preparation version into its shard.json, and the distribution declaration lists them in identicalAcrossShards.
reproducibilityChecklist.why: verify --shards then refuses a merge over shards that disagree on any of them

reproducibilityChecklist.cost: deterministic kernels can run slower and some operations raise instead of running; measure the pilot with the flags on
reproducibilityChecklist.rule: Set torch.manual_seed(seed) per unit, torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True), CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8 and torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False.
reproducibilityChecklist.why: GPU kernels are otherwise free to reorder floating-point sums

reproducibilityChecklist.rule: Every notebook mounts the same official dataset version and reads the one official preparation (datasets/<slug>/splits.json).
reproducibilityChecklist.why: a shard on another data version answers another question

reproducibilityChecklist.rule: Rehearse once per account before any campaign: readiness is per worker and never carries over from another account.
reproducibilityChecklist.why: a missing secret or quota on one account fails only that account's shards

reproducibilityChecklist.rule: Never pool wall time or memory across machines; they are perEnvironment measurements.
reproducibilityChecklist.why: an average over two machines describes neither

reproducibilityChecklist.rule: One account per person per service: every participating account is owned and operated by a distinct team member registered with `smith team`, and parallelism counts distinct owners, never accounts. On Colab only paid compute (Pro, Pay-As-You-Go compute units, Enterprise) joins a split campaign; where a service's terms are unverified the same one-per-person rule applies.
reproducibilityChecklist.why: several accounts held by one person to get around per-user limits are a terms violation, not an optimisation

reproducibilityChecklist.rule: Run one campaign on one service; mix services only when the shards' environment stamps (accelerator model, CUDA, torch) are declared identical, and let verify --shards confirm it.
reproducibilityChecklist.why: two services rarely hand out the same accelerator and software, and a merge over different stamps is several experiments

reproducibilityChecklist.rule: The verdict is never launch authorization: placement stays with distribute and the launch with submit behind the operator's consent.
reproducibilityChecklist.why: a campaign is hours of somebody's quota
